$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.2 & 0.1 \\ 0.3 & 0.2 & 0.65 \\ 0.3 & 0.6 & 0.25\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above, what is the value of $a+b-c?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14235560/assets/dc38bc15beeeb04b5402dbcf559ec5acdc1b321c712c61f1edcef65da542ac57.svg)

Find the steady-state vector $\mathbf q$ of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above.
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $\mathbf{q}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14235560/assets/63be10f14754ed79801a48f62598ac770928df77409bb30b9534e69e6123d732.svg)

The matrix equation $(P-I)\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{0}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.9 & 0.3 & 0.5 & 0 \\ 0.2 & -0.7 & 0.1 & 0 \\ 0.7 & 0.4 & -0.6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=20{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=20{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & 6 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 14 & 8 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ -18 & 6 & 10 & 0 \\ 14 & 8 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+9{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-7{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -57 & 19 & 0 \\ 0 & 57 & -19 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -57 & 19 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
x_2=\dfrac{1}{3}x_3.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2x_1 -7\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x_3\right) + x_3 = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = \dfrac{2}{3}x_3.
$$

Hence, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14235560/assets/1cbbad8b2f59addb1eef5983219b6875f066c9cc351bb15925544dc1e5be4bfd.svg)

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ 2{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, our steady-state vector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14235560/assets/6c681cf1078c38dbb876a77bd6c060b3528fa91bcc398c5ca395f440ec683a27.svg)
